goal: We need configurable timeouts end to end: the transport currently hard-codes a 1s deadline and every caller inherits it. Add a `timeout` parameter (default 1.0) to the transport's send(), thread it through the client's fetch(), and make sure BOTH call sites (the service sync and the bulk exporter) can pass their own timeout down. Existing callers without the argument must keep working.

hows.text: Implement a centralized timeout configuration via a dedicated settings module, injecting the timeout parameter into the transport layer and threading it through the client and service layers to ensure all call sites can pass their own values.
hows.reason: This approach provides maximum flexibility and clean separation of concerns, allowing for centralized, easily configurable timeout management across the entire application stack.

hows.text: Introduce a dynamic timeout resolution strategy using a configurable base timeout, allowing callers to override it directly at the service and bulk exporter levels while maintaining backward compatibility for existing hard-coded calls.
hows.reason: This approach offers robust adaptability for varying execution needs, ensuring the transport can dynamically handle different timeout requirements without disrupting existing callers.
